subject: Tenant-level retention & storage residency: clarification and next steps
messages:
From: Marie Brun <marie.brun@acme-robotics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme-robotics.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Questions on tenant-level retention & EU residency controls

Hi Sean,

Hope you’re well. As we prepare for our internal audit, a couple of quick questions about Redwood’s tenant-level retention and regional storage controls for customers in the EU: 

1) Can we configure per-tenant retention windows (e.g., 90/180/730 days) that are enforced server-side and visible to our admins?
2) Is it possible to pin a tenant’s data to an EU-only storage region (not just processing in-region) and ensure backups/replicas also remain within the EU?
3) If a user requests erasure at the tenant level, what is the expected delete workflow and timeline (soft delete -> purge)? Do you provide audit evidence for completed erasures?

If you can send a short checklist or the relevant design note, that would be great. We’re targeting a compliance sign-off by mid-January and want to align on feasibility and timeline.

Thanks,
Marie
Marie Brun
Head of Compliance, Acme Robotics
[Attachment: compliance-scope.pdf (PDF)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Marie Brun <marie.brun@acme-robotics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 10:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Questions on tenant-level retention & EU residency controls

Marie — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: yes to configurable tenant retention windows, yes to EU-only residency for primary + replicas (with caveats), and yes we provide an auditable erase workflow.

I’ve attached a short checklist that maps the features to compliance evidence and called out where we need to confirm implementation details with engineering.

Proposed next step: 30-min sync next week to walk the checklist and capture any account-specific constraints. Monica (AM) — can you coordinate a slot? Karthik, I’m looping you for the technical confirm on cross-region backups and final purge guarantees.

Best,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: retention-checklist.pdf (PDF)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marie Brun <marie.brun@acme-robotics.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2027 15:23:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Questions on tenant-level retention & EU residency controls

Marie/Sean — adding more detail from the engineering side so you have the constraints before the call.

- Retention windows: We support per-tenant retention TTLs at the control plane level. Admins can select from preset buckets (30/90/180/365/730) or request a custom SLA. Enforcement is server-side and logged; deletions propagate to object storage via a background purge job.

- Residency and replicas: We offer "EU-only" tenancy by creating tenant storage in EU regions and restricting replica placement. However, some managed services (e.g., cross-region metadata index) may still require metadata routing—these are logically partitioned and encrypted with customer KMS. We can provide a configuration that avoids sending PII-containing payloads outside the EU.

- Erasure workflow: Soft-delete flag applied immediately; user-facing resources are hidden within seconds. Full purge depends on replication window and compaction cycles — typically completes within 72 hours for active shards in EU-only tenants. We emit a signed audit record when purge completes (timestamp, operator, job id).

Open engineering clarifications we need from Acme:
- Do you require admin UI controls for retention changes or will API-based controls be sufficient?
- Any expectation around instantaneous purge for legal holds vs standard erasure?

I’ve pasted a link to the internal design doc with the planned APIs and audit event schema: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/tenant-retention-design-v2

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Product Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marie Brun <marie.brun@acme-robotics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme-robotics.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 08:40:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Questions on tenant-level retention & EU residency controls

Thanks Karthik — that helps a lot. A couple follow-ups:

- API controls are fine for now, but we’ll need an admin UI before GA; can you provide an ETA for that?
- For legal holds: when a hold is placed we need data to be non-purgeable until the hold is removed. If purge windows are 72 hours, that’s acceptable provided legal-hold overrides are instantaneous.
- Audit evidence: the signed audit record is critical. Can you include a sample PDF report we can drop into our audit packet?

We’re happy to take the checklist to our internal stakeholders; can you also provide a simple mutual action plan (MAP) that shows milestones (design confirm, staging test, GA opt-in) and an estimated timeline? Target: compliance sign-off by 2028-01-15.

Best,
Marie

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Marie Brun <marie.brun@acme-robotics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2027 16:45:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Questions on tenant-level retention & EU residency controls

Marie — great, we can align to that sign-off window. Attached is a draft MAP with milestones and owner points, and I asked engineering to include a sample audit PDF in our staging artifact. High level timeline in the MAP:

- Week of 2027-12-13: design confirmation and tenant configuration sign-off (Redwood + Acme)
- Week of 2027-12-20: staging enablement (EU tenant created, sample purge/audit run)
- Week of 2028-01-03: final audit evidence delivered and partner sign-off testing
- Week of 2028-01-10: GA opt-in window opens (customer toggles to enable)

Monica — please own scheduling the design sync and tracking the MAP milestones in HubSpot. I’ll follow up with the sample audit PDF and the MAP attachment.

Thanks all — we’ll get you the PDF and spreadsheet by EOD.

Best,
Sean
[Attachment: MAP-Acme-20271209.xlsx (Excel)]
